---
title: GitHub Actions
description: Run web, iOS, and Android tests on GitHub Actions, upload the reports, and post the results on the pull request.
icon: "/images/icons/github-actions.svg"
---

This page has two workflows: one for web targets and one for iOS and
Android targets. Read the [CI overview](/ci) first. It tells you what CI
mode changes, how to give the job model credentials, and what each exit
code means.

## Web

This workflow runs deterministic and agent tests in the same job. It
assumes that your config has a [command](/web#starting-your-app) that starts
the app, and that AI Gateway does the model calls:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/e2e.yml" expandable
name: e2e

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install browsers
        run: pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps

      - name: Run e2e
        run: npx e2e run --reporter list,junit
        env:
          APP_URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Upload report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: e2e-report
          path: |
            .e2e/report.json
            .e2e/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts
          path: .e2e/results
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7
```

The workflow pins each action to a commit SHA and installs the dependencies
from the lockfile. `npx e2e` runs the installed version. The
[install command](/reference/web#installing-browsers) downloads the browsers
for the Playwright version that the engine pins, with their system
libraries.

The upload steps run on each run that is not cancelled. So a test that
failed and then passed on retry keeps its evidence.

## iOS and Android

This workflow has two jobs, one for each platform. Before you use it, read
[Mobile jobs](/ci#mobile-jobs). That section tells you what each job needs
on every CI service.

The iOS job builds the app for the simulator with `xcodebuild`. You can use
a different build command. The command must write a simulator `.app` and
must not start the app. For Expo, `npx expo run:ios --configuration Release
--device generic --no-bundler --output build/ios` builds without a
simulator and writes the `.app` under `build/ios`.

```yaml title=".github/workflows/e2e-mobile.yml" expandable
name: e2e mobile

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  ios:
    runs-on: macos-26
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: pod install
        working-directory: ios

      - name: Build for the simulator
        run: |
          xcodebuild -workspace ios/MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp \
            -configuration Release -sdk iphonesimulator \
            -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
            -derivedDataPath build
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.agent-device
          key: agent-device-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Boot a simulator and install the app
        run: |
          UDID=$(xcrun simctl create e2e "iPhone 17" com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimRuntime.iOS-26-5)
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$UDID" -b
          xcrun simctl install "$UDID" build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app

      - run: npx e2e run --target ios --reporter list,junit
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: e2e-ios
          path: .e2e
          if-no-files-found: warn

  android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: npm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      # React Native and Expo templates sign release builds with the debug keystore.
      - name: Build the APK
        run: cd android && ./gradlew :app:assembleRelease

      - name: Run on an emulator
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 36
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          profile: pixel_7
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
            npx e2e run --target android --reporter list,junit
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: e2e-android
          path: .e2e
          if-no-files-found: warn
```

The emulator runner action boots the emulator and runs each `script` line
in a new shell. When the step ends, the action stops the emulator. So the
install and the run must be in the same step.

This repository runs its own mobile suites this way. See
[`mobile.yml`](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/main/.github/workflows/mobile.yml)
for a version that does these things:

- It caches the Expo build for each native fingerprint.
- It boots two simulators for two workers.
- It runs the failed tests again with `--last-failed`.

## Pull request comments

Add the [`@e2e-dev/github` reporter](/github) to post the results of each
job as one comment on the pull request. A rerun updates the same comment.
The reporter also writes the results to the job summary. The workflows
above have read-only permissions. To post, the job needs `pull-requests: write` and
`GITHUB_TOKEN` in the env of the test step. See [Setup](/github#setup).
GitHub gives a read-only token to a `pull_request` run from a fork, so the
reporter cannot post there. See
[When nothing is posted](/github#when-nothing-is-posted).

To block a merge on a failed run, make the e2e job a required check in the
repository settings.

## Secrets

Keep the model key in a repository secret, as the workflows above do.
GitHub does not give secrets to pull requests from forks. See
[Model credentials](/ci#model-credentials).

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Pull request comments" icon="code-pull-request" href="/github">
    One comment per run, edited in place on a rerun.
  </Card>
  <Card title="CI overview" icon="rotate" href="/ci">
    CI defaults, sharding, reruns, and exit codes.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

---
title: Decision models
description: Run bounded actions with a decision model and a small text model instead of a full LLM agent.
icon: "scale-balanced"
---

`@e2e-dev/decision` runs `agent.act` and `agent.assert` through a decision
model instead of an LLM. For each action the decision model answers one
request: which operation, and which element for each operation that has
more than one, chosen from what the executor builds out of the latest
semantic tree. It never generates free text: when the choice is `type`, a
small language model writes the field value. Both models are
plain AI SDK models, so any decision model provider that answers `choice`
questions with probability distributions (Jev) and any language-model
provider works; the runner still authorizes every dispatched action.

## Install and configure

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npm install -D @e2e-dev/decision
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm add -D @e2e-dev/decision
```

```bash bun
bun add -d @e2e-dev/decision
```
</CodeGroup>

The decision model answers `choice` questions with probability
distributions; the text model writes field values. Each installs as its
own package. Decision models need `ai` 7, version 7.0.128 or later:

<CodeGroup>
```bash npm
npm install -D @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider
```

```bash pnpm
pnpm add -D @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider
```

```bash bun
bun add -d @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider
```
</CodeGroup>

```ts title="e2e.config.ts"
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { decisionExecutor } from '@e2e-dev/decision';
import { typeSafeAi } from '@ai-sdk/typesafe-ai';
import { openrouter } from '@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider';

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://localhost:3000' } }],
  agents: {
    default: {
      executor: decisionExecutor({
        model: typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest'),
        textModel: openrouter('inception/mercury-2.5'),
      }),
    },
  },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

`evaluationModel()` instances still work. A model id string or a language
model in `model` fails config load with `INVALID_CONFIG`.

Tests stay plain natural language, with no params needed:

```ts title="tests/todos.e2e.ts"
import { test, expect } from 'e2e';

test('adds a todo', async ({ app, screen, agent }) => {
  await app.open('/todos');
  await agent.act('Add a todo named Buy coffee, and verify it is listed.');
  await expect(screen.getByTestId('todo')).toContainText('Buy coffee');
  await agent.assert('The todo list contains Buy coffee.');
});
```

## How text gets typed

The decision model only ever names an element index. When it picks `type`,
the text model writes the value from the goal, the field's label, and the
page text, and the executor types exactly that string. Model output never
becomes a selector, a URL, or a key. When the goal supplies no value,
nothing is typed and the decision model picks another action. Password
fields never reach the text model; secrets stay declared handles that only
`typeSecret` fills.

The text model is also the agent's judgment tier: it is exposed as the
executor's `model`, so `waitFor` and `extract` use it too. It can come
from the agents entry's `model` instead. Without either, `type` is never
offered.

## Finishing a step

When the decision model answers `done` or `failed`, the executor checks
the claim on a fresh screen with one question: is the step's task complete?
It sees the step's non-secret params, the actions taken with the non-secret
values typed, and the page, including the text of named status regions, but
no model reasoning or secret. A confirmed `done` passes the
step and a confirmed `failed` fails it with `ACTION_FAILED`. An
unconfirmed claim goes back to the decision model as history; the second one
ends the step, as `ACTION_FAILED` when the screen contradicts the goal and
as `blocked` (`AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`) otherwise.

## Gates

Both gates are off by default: the executor follows the most probable
choice. Set `minProbability` or `minConfidence` to block weaker actions,
reject weaker completion checks, and fail weaker assertions as
inconclusive instead:

```ts title="Executor setup"
const executor = decisionExecutor({ model, minProbability: 0.9, minConfidence: 0.8 });
```

Probability and confidence are different provider fields: probability is the
selected option's share of the answer distribution, confidence is the
provider's separate statistic. A threshold is a policy choice; measure
accuracy on your own tests before changing it.

## Provider options

`providerOptions` go with every decide call, the completion checks
included. Use them for options of the decision model's provider, such as
zero data retention on Vercel AI Gateway:

```ts title="Executor setup"
import { gateway } from 'ai';

const executor = decisionExecutor({
  model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev'),
  textModel: gateway('openai/gpt-4.1-nano'),
  providerOptions: { gateway: { zeroDataRetention: true } },
});
```

They reach the decision model only. The text model takes the agents
entry's `providerOptions`, so a gateway setting meant for one model, such as
a fallback list, never reaches the other.

## Limits

- No vision: screenshots never reach the model; canvas-only controls and
  image-based targets are not implemented.
- No `navigate`: in-app navigation is a `tap` on a link. URLs belong in
  test code (`browser.goto`, `app.open`).
- No multi-select `listbox` in v1.
- The choice cap is 255 options per question (TypeSafe's limit). Larger
  screens list viewport nodes first and count the rest as omitted, so the
  model can scroll; the step never blocks just for being large.
- Drag, upload, and hover are not offered in v1.
- `waitFor` and `extract` use the text model through the runner's
  built-in judgment tier.

name: agent

# The agent suites spend real model calls, so they cannot gate every PR. They
# are the only thing that exercises `agent-protocol-1` against a real provider
# instead of tests/helpers/fake-model.ts, so they run on a schedule instead of
# never.
on:
  schedule:
    # Mondays 04:17 UTC. Off the hour to avoid the scheduler's peak backlog.
    - cron: '17 4 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      suite:
        description: 'Which suite to run'
        required: false
        default: all
        type: choice
        options: [all, agent, dogfood]
      model:
        description: 'Override the testbed model id (E2E_MODEL, e.g. openai/gpt-5.4-mini, served by the Vercel AI Gateway)'
        required: false
        type: string

# The repository's own runs are not usage: the CLI sends no telemetry from CI here.
env:
  E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # A manual run picks one suite or all of them. Selecting here rather than
  # skipping steps inside the matrix keeps unselected suites out of the run
  # entirely, so the checks list shows what actually ran.
  plan:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.select.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - name: Select suites
        id: select
        env:
          # Empty on schedule, which means every suite.
          SUITE: ${{ inputs.suite }}
        run: |
          # Both suites run against local deterministic apps, so a failure
          # is ours: the playground (act flows + judgments) and the dogfood
          # expense app (custom executor tools through the config).
          all='[
            {"suite":"agent","script":"test:agent","optional":false},
            {"suite":"dogfood","script":"test:dogfood","optional":false}
          ]'
          if [ -z "$SUITE" ] || [ "$SUITE" = all ]; then
            selected=$(echo "$all" | jq -c .)
          else
            selected=$(echo "$all" | jq -c --arg s "$SUITE" '[.[] | select(.suite == $s)]')
          fi
          if [ "$(echo "$selected" | jq 'length')" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::unknown suite \"$SUITE\""
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "matrix=$selected" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  agent:
    needs: plan
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      # One suite failing must not hide the other's result.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    name: ${{ matrix.suite }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      # A missing credential fails every agent fixture with MODEL_UNAVAILABLE,
      # which reads as a product defect. Say what is actually wrong instead.
      - name: Require model credential
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY is not set for this repository." \
              "The agent suites need a real provider credential."
            exit 1
          fi
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Install browsers
        run: pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec playwright-core install chromium --with-deps
      - name: Build
        run: pnpm run build
      - name: Run ${{ matrix.script }}
        continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.optional }}
        env:
          # Every testbed config builds its model with the AI SDK's gateway(), which reads this variable.
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
          # Read through a variable, not interpolated into the script, and left
          # unset when empty: the configs treat '' as a configured model id.
          MODEL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.model }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$MODEL_INPUT" ]; then
            export E2E_MODEL="$MODEL_INPUT"
          fi
          pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed run ${{ matrix.script }}
      # The JSON report is the only durable evidence of a model-dependent run.
      # A storage quota that refuses the upload must not turn a green suite red;
      # on the weekly schedule two weeks of retention is two runs.
      - name: Upload report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: agent-report-${{ matrix.suite }}
          path: apps/testbed/.e2e/report.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

{

name: spec

# The ruleset requires `spec gate` alone, so a job added here gates merges
# once it is listed in the gate's `needs`.
on:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# The repository's own runs are not usage: the CLI sends no telemetry from CI here.
env:
  E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Lint
        run: pnpm lint
      - name: Dead code (fallow)
        run: pnpm check:dead-code
      - name: Typecheck packages
        run: pnpm typecheck
      - name: Error code reference
        run: pnpm docs:check-errors
      - name: Peer ranges on the runner
        run: pnpm check:peer-ranges
      - name: No install scripts in published dependency trees
        run: pnpm check:install-scripts
      - name: Agent skill scripts
        run: |
          pnpm exec tsc -p .dev/skills/babysit/scripts
          node --test .dev/skills/babysit/scripts/pr-status.test.ts
      - name: Install browsers
        run: node packages/web/dist/bin.js install chromium --with-deps
      - name: Testbed
        run: pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/testbed test

  test:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The newest release of each line, and the floors in engines.node.
        node: [22, 24, 26, 22.22.3, 24.8.0]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          # A major alone resolves to the runner's cached release, which can
          # sit below the patch floor in engines.node (22.22.3).
          check-latest: true
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Install browsers
        run: pnpm --filter @e2e-dev/web exec playwright-core install chromium --with-deps
      - name: Unit and integration tests
        run: pnpm test

  # A new user's first install of the packed packages, which pnpm 11 and
  # later fail on any dependency build script (scripts/install-smoke.ts).
  install:
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        pnpm: [11, 12]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 26
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm run build
      - name: Fresh install with pnpm ${{ matrix.pnpm }}
        run: node scripts/install-smoke.ts ${{ matrix.pnpm }}

  # The one check the ruleset requires from this workflow. A skipped job
  # passes (the change cannot reach it); a failed or cancelled one fails it.
  gate:
    name: spec gate
    needs: [check, test, install]
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Require every job to pass or skip
        env:
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: |
          failed="$(jq -r '[to_entries[] | select(.value.result != "success" and .value.result != "skipped") | "\(.key) \(.value.result)"] | join(", ")' <<< "$RESULTS")"
          [ -z "$failed" ] || { echo "::error::$failed"; exit 1; }

/**
 * The agent's vocabulary by name: the tools the grammar hands a model, and
 * the names an agent step's engine events carry for what the dispatcher did.
 * Telemetry counts an agent's actions by these names and nothing else, so
 * adding an action means adding it here. A leaf module, so config resolution
 * can check a project tool's name without loading the grammar.
 */

/** The name of each grammar action, as the dispatcher records it. */
export const GRAMMAR_ACTION_NAMES = [
  'back',
  'check',
  'dismissKeyboard',
  'doubleTap',
  'dragTo',
  'hover',
  'hoverAt',
  'longPress',
  'navigate',
  'press',
  'pressKey',
  'scroll',
  'scrollIntoView',
  'scrollUntil',
  'secondaryTap',
  'selectOption',
  'setInputFiles',
  'tap',
  'tapAt',
  'type',
  'typeSecret',
  'typeText',
  'uncheck',
] as const;

/** One name of the vocabulary; what the dispatcher records an action under, so a new verb cannot slip past telemetry. */
export type GrammarActionName = (typeof GRAMMAR_ACTION_NAMES)[number];

/** The prefix of the engine event a project's own tool records; its name is the project's, and telemetry folds it away. */
export const PROJECT_TOOL_EVENT_PREFIX = 'tool:';

/**
 * The tools the harness adds beside the grammar, each where it adds them:
 * `complete_step` in every agent step, `locate` and the recording tools in
 * an `e2e mcp` session, and `report_finding` under `e2e explore`. A project
 * tool named like one would be replaced or dropped there, so the config load
 * refuses the name.
 */
export const HARNESS_TOOL_NAMES: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map([
  ['complete_step', 'every agent step'],
  ['locate', 'an e2e mcp session'],
  ['start_recording', 'an e2e mcp session'],
  ['stop_recording', 'an e2e mcp session'],
  ['report_finding', 'e2e explore'],
]);

/**
